target:
def Target : Prop :=
  ∀ (T : ℕ) (N : S1 Bool Bool), N.D9 → S1.D5 T N d15 → T ≤ N.d13
a_raw: {"translation":"Target defines, but does not prove, the following proposition. For every natural number T and every system N with Boolean inputs and Boolean outputs, suppose first that no index of N has a nonempty directed path of dependencies back to itself (even a single self-edge is forbidden). There is an edge from m to n if there exist two complete state assignments and one Boolean input such that the assignments agree at every index other than m, but the update at n gives different values for the two assignments on that same input. The assignments need not be reachable from the initial state. Suppose next that for every Boolean list of length at most T, the output of N, starting from its initial assignment and updating all indices together on each input from left to right, equals the output of d15: true if the list contains true, and false otherwise. This includes the empty list and requires no agreement on longer lists. Then T is at most the number of indices in N.A1."}
translation: Target defines, but does not prove, the following proposition. For every natural number T and every system N with Boolean inputs and Boolean outputs, suppose first that no index of N has a nonempty directed path of dependencies back to itself (even a single self-edge is forbidden). There is an edge from m to n if there exist two complete state assignments and one Boolean input such that the assignments agree at every index other than m, but the update at n gives different values for the two assignments on that same input. The assignments need not be reachable from the initial state. Suppose next that for every Boolean list of length at most T, the output of N, starting from its initial assignment and updating all indices together on each input from left to right, equals the output of d15: true if the list contains true, and false otherwise. This includes the empty list and requires no agreement on longer lists. Then T is at most the number of indices in N.A1.

divergences.description: Counting copies in a construction is not a lower bound on every implementation. For a one-unit network, one copy per timestep gives an unrolling with T units. The TARGET says that no functionally equivalent feedforward system can use fewer, whether or not it is built by unrolling. Neither the copy count nor the qualified observation that feedforward networks generally need more neurons establishes that necessity.
The TARGET selects a particular function: a single initially false Boolean unit records whether any input so far has been true. Neither passage identifies this function or a one-unit example.

The TARGET specifies finite-horizon equivalence as exact output agreement on every Boolean list of length at most T, including the empty list, with no requirement on longer lists. The passages do not specify this test for functional equivalence.

The TARGET counts state indices as neurons and defines feedforwardness by acyclicity of update dependencies tested on all state assignments, even unreachable ones. These are modeling choices, not criteria given in the passages.

judgement.summary: The TARGET captures the author's proposed lower bound for the Boolean example, but that bound is an additional claim. The sources describe the size of the network produced by unrolling and a general tendency toward larger feedforward networks, not a minimum size for every equivalent network.
